defects: Hypothesis is stronger than gold's: `(List.filter p l).length ≤ 1` requires at most one *position* in the list to satisfy p, whereas gold's `{x ∈ l₁ | p x}.Subsingleton` only requires at most one *distinct value* satisfying p (duplicates of the same satisfying element are allowed). E.g. l = [1,1,2] with p x = (x == 1): filter length = 2 (fails produced hypothesis) but the set {x | x ∈ l ∧ p x} = {1} is a subsingleton (satisfies gold hypothesis), and the conclusion still holds. So the produced statement is a strictly narrower special case, not equivalent to the gold theorem.
